title: 1986 AHSME Problem 15
statement: A student attempted to compute the average, \(A,\) of \(x,\) \(y\) and \(z\) by computing the average of \(x\) and \(y,\) and then computing the average of the result and \(z.\) Whenever \(x\lt y\lt z,\) the student’s final result is

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: sometimes less than \(A\) and sometimes equal to \(A\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: sometimes greater than \(A\) and sometimes equal to \(A\)

solutions.text:
The student’s result is \(\frac{x+y+2z}{4},\) while the true average is \(\frac{x+y+z}{3}.\) Their difference is \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{x+y+2z}{4}-\frac{x+y+z}{3}\\ &\qquad=\frac{2z-x-y}{12}. \end{aligned} \] Since \(z\gt x\) and \(z\gt y,\) the numerator is positive. The student’s result is therefore always greater than \(A.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Write both the true average and the student’s result as algebraic expressions
Subtract the true average and use the order \(x\lt y\lt z\) to determine the sign
